intent: To demonstrate that the rate of battle deaths has decreased over time, supporting the idea that war is going out of fashion.

units.meaning: Battle deaths per million declined substantially from 1950 to 2014, showing a long-term downward trend.
accepted_routes: battle deaths per million fell from about 195 in 1950 to about 2.5 in 2014
the rate of battle deaths declined across the 1950–2014 period
war-related deaths per million trended downward from the early 1950s to 2014
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show the series starting near 195 at 1950 and ending near 2.5 at 2014, with an overall downward envelope across the timeline.
units.temporal_anchor: war actually seems to be going out of fashion
units.reviewer_question: Is the overall 1950-to-2014 downward trend required, or can the clip show only a local decline?

units.meaning: The 2014 battle-death rate was about 192.4 deaths per million lower than the 1950 rate, a reduction of about 98.7%.
accepted_routes: battle deaths per million dropped by roughly 192 from 1950 to 2014
the 2014 rate was about 98.7% lower than the 1950 rate
units.visual_evidence_rule: First and last values must be annotated or linked so the total drop and/or percentage reduction can be read.
units.temporal_anchor: war actually seems to be going out of fashion
units.reviewer_question: Should the clip explicitly quantify the total decline, or only imply it via the two endpoint values?

units.meaning: The highest battle-death rate in the series occurred in 1950 at 194.9 deaths per million.
accepted_routes: the peak battle-death rate was about 195 per million in 1950
the series starts at its maximum, 194.9 in 1950
1950 had the highest battle deaths per million, 194.9
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 1950 point must be visible as the highest point on the chart.
units.temporal_anchor: if you look at the numbers
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip identify 1950 as the maximum, or is the starting high value enough?

units.meaning: The decline was not monotonic: after 1950, the rate rebounded to a secondary peak of 86.9 deaths per million in 1974 before falling again.
accepted_routes: there was a secondary peak of about 87 deaths per million in 1974
the decline was interrupted by a 1970s rebound to 86.9
after falling from 1950, the rate rose again to 86.9 in 1974
units.visual_evidence_rule: If included, a local bump around 1974 must be visible on the chart.
units.temporal_anchor: if you look at the numbers
units.reviewer_question: Should the video acknowledge the 1970s rebound, or is a simplified downward trend acceptable?

units.meaning: The series reached its lowest rate in 2012 and 2013 at 0.8 deaths per million.
accepted_routes: the lowest rate was 0.8 deaths per million in 2012 and 2013
the series reached its minimum of 0.8 in 2012–2013
by 2012–2013 battle deaths per million had fallen below 1
units.visual_evidence_rule: The minimum point(s) around 2012–2013 must be visible or labeled if this unit is included.
units.temporal_anchor: war actually seems to be going out of fashion
units.reviewer_question: Should the clip explicitly identify the minimum, or is the low endpoint value enough?

optional_valid: Other local peaks such as 1971 (65.0), 1973 (62.4), 1986 (49.8), and 1993 (44.7) could be shown as fluctuations.
The sharp 1993-to-1994 drop from 44.7 to 17.7 could be annotated as another notable fall.
The temporary low around 2001–2003 (7.6, 5.9, 5.9) could be shown before the later 2009–2013 decline.
unsupported_to_avoid: Global population being at an all-time high, since population data is not in the table.
Any causal claim that population growth or specific wars caused the decline.
Extrapolating beyond 2014 or predicting that war will disappear.
Interpreting relative_value as a share of all deaths or using an unstated denominator.
Comparisons to other causes of death, countries, or conflicts not present in the table.
notes: The table contains one series, battle deaths per million, from 1950–2014; the narration's population clause is not supported by the table. Derived values use only the 1950 and 2014 table cells.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
